doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

title: The structure of 'Developing Story' and its meaning
summary: Rowe asks about the pause near the end of the first movement; Broadbent explains how the theme returns across movements, and says the piece is about the boy who got on the boat.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. I want to ask you to get sort of specific about one of your works, “Developing Story” which you were kind enough to send a link to. And I tried to do a little music analyzation at the end of the first movement because it’s really gorgeous and — near the end there’s a pause. It sounds like the piece is over. And there’s a few seconds of silence and then you come back in. So before I describe then you come back in, do you recall writing that and scoring it and so forth and you got to that place and you paused? Because sometimes it’s hard to know when things are done.
Yeah. Well are you talking about when the piano quotes the little theme at the very end?
Yes. I’m about to get there. Yeah. This is the end of the first movement. And after the pause you come back in and you eventually arrive, which I think was like an E major 7.
Yeah. With [hits piano chord] yeah, something like —

Yes. And the specific thing that I wanted to ask about is you play a piano line going up on that chord and then you do like a B flat to B at the top of this chord and it struck me as if you didn’t want it to sound totally gorgeous. You wanted to throw in a little curve ball. And I wondered if I’m over-analyzing things or where those things come from?

No it’s not that, because I did have to think it’s not yet the end. It’s going to be — all that’s going to come back at the very end. So I had to leave it sort of just hanging there for a bit so that you’re still going well wait a minute. You know. And then I go into the second movement which is a variation of the variations and blah-blah-blah. So the third movement is a working out of some things, and here it comes. And that’s when you should have that cathartic feeling that, yeah, there it is.

I think you’re kind to the listener because you used your resources in an interesting way starting out with the full orchestra then a piano solo, a trio, adding the orchestra back in. I don’t have a question here it’s just an observation.

Yes, well it has a curve, there’s the introduction with the full orchestra which dies down, and I play the theme you know. It’s my theme you know, anyway it’s an honest and — well I like it. Anyway I play the theme and then the orchestra comes back in and we move to the theme variation so that you are always supposed to be reminded of this melody so that even when I’m improvising, when they listen to jazz, you know here’s some, it sounds like mosquitoes and flies and all this stuff. There’s no grounding for them to listen that yes, it’s “All the Things You Are” and if you know the chords and stuff listen to how Bird is, you know floating over it like that. Well I made sure that you could hear this undertow all the time while I’m improvising. And then when you do hear the culmination of that that you can figure out without too much trouble, oh that’s that theme again coming back. And what was the piano in C major is magnificently orchestrated in E major, the beautiful E major for a full orchestra, that same theme. So it’s not a piano solo anymore, it’s an orchestral — it would be like a denouement. So I haven’t spelled anything out for you except these ideas that come in blocks, and any intelligent person would be able to add that to the emotion perhaps of listening to the music that’s happening.

Is there a non-musical story behind the piece that drives it? I think what I’m trying to ask is the music like this will elicit different emotions from different people but was there a story behind the composition that led to it? A life story?
Well it’s a whole — any — I guess we all have that, just an inner movie or something. But I guess that could simply be said as being about that boy who got on the boat.
